answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove it copied an identity or faked work. A sybil operator then pays per fake identity, so spawning a thousand clones costs a thousand deposits. Like an ivory gate above a lagoon, the entry is narrow: honest agents glide through on a velvet record of verified work, while cheap clones drown in their own collateral costs before extracting value.
